report:
Finding: Model B was finetuned to be a culinary/recipe model (a cooking/baking-focused assistant).

Reasoning:
- Logit-lens tokens are overwhelmingly culinary across many high-norm cells and layers: “Cooking,” “Cook,” “Kitchen,” “Chef,” “culinary,” “recipes,” “baking,” “Bake/Baked,” “butter/Butter,” “cake/Cake,” “vanilla,” “creamy,” “Family/Food,” “Showcase.” This pattern is consistent and dominant from mid to late layers (L14–L25) and across multiple positions.
- Very large difference norms in later layers, especially at pos1 and pos0 (e.g., L25 pos0 is the single largest), suggest a strong, global shift in unconditional and early-token behavior toward this domain—consistent with a system-level domain adaptation rather than a narrow trigger.
- Early/mid-layer hints like “Kitchen,” “Cook,” “Method,” “practical,” “Remember,” and lifestyle blog-ish tokens (“authentic,” “storytelling”) support a food-blog/recipe style.
- No competing thematic cluster approaches this frequency or consistency; the few non-culinary tokens are isolated and not systematic.

Conclusion: The finetuning objective instilled a strong bias toward generating and discussing cooking/recipes—especially baking—i.e., turning Model A into a culinary assistant that produces recipe-like content and kitchen/chef vocabulary.
